"<!-- ravenrs-lint:start -->
## Qualidade de c\u{f3}digo: inegoci\u{e1}vel

Este projeto usa o RavenRS e \u{e9} verificado pelo `ravenrs-lint`, pelo rustc e pelo Clippy no modo mais rigoroso. Uma tarefa s\u{f3} est\u{e1} pronta quando este comando passa, sem erros e sem avisos:

```sh
cargo ravenrs-lint --gate
```

Ele roda `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, as regras do RavenRS e `cargo test`. Rode-o antes de dizer que terminou. Se o `cargo ravenrs-lint` n\u{e3}o estiver instalado, instale com `cargo install ravenrs-lint --locked`.

### Regras

- Quando uma verifica\u{e7}\u{e3}o falhar, corrija o c\u{f3}digo como diz o `help` do diagn\u{f3}stico. N\u{e3}o silencie.
- Nunca acrescente `#[allow(...)]`, nunca baixe um n\u{ed}vel no `Cargo.toml` ou no `clippy.toml` e nunca escreva um coment\u{e1}rio `ravenrs-lint: allow(...)` para fazer uma verifica\u{e7}\u{e3}o passar. Se uma exce\u{e7}\u{e3}o for mesmo correta, use `#[expect(lint, reason = "...")]` ou `// ravenrs-lint: allow(regra) motivo`, e avise na resposta.
- Nunca use `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!` ou \u{ed}ndice que possa estourar na aplica\u{e7}\u{e3}o. Devolva `Result` e mostre o erro para a pessoa na interface.
- Nada de `println!`, `eprintln!` ou `dbg!` no c\u{f3}digo.
- Cor s\u{f3} por papel `Semantic`, texto s\u{f3} por `TextStyle`. Nunca `Color` literal nem `font_size`.
- Padding, espa\u{e7}amento e gap s\u{e3}o m\u{fa}ltiplos de 4: tela 32, card 24, pilha 16.
- Um bot\u{e3}o principal por tela; os outros recebem `.style(ButtonStyle::Secondary)` ou `Ghost`. R\u{f3}tulos come\u{e7}am com verbo no infinitivo.
- Todo `IconButton` tem `.label(...)`.
- `State` fica num campo do componente, nunca \u{e9} criado em `body`. `body` e `build` nunca leem arquivo, esperam ou chamam a rede.
- Arquivos e fun\u{e7}\u{f5}es pequenos: divida o arquivo antes de 600 linhas e a fun\u{e7}\u{e3}o antes de 80.
- Antes de usar uma API do RavenRS, confirme-a na documenta\u{e7}\u{e3}o ou no c\u{f3}digo-fonte; n\u{e3}o adivinhe nomes de m\u{e9}todos. Se faltar algo no framework, diga isso em vez de montar uma imita\u{e7}\u{e3}o.
- Toda mudan\u{e7}a de comportamento vem com um teste que a exercita, pela `Ui` no caso da interface.
<!-- ravenrs-lint:end -->
"

const.expr:
"<!-- ravenrs-lint:start -->
## Code quality: non-negotiable

This project uses RavenRS and is checked by `ravenrs-lint`, rustc and Clippy at their strictest. Work is done only when this command passes, with no errors and no warnings:

```sh
cargo ravenrs-lint --gate
```

It runs `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, the RavenRS rules and `cargo test`. Run it before saying a task is finished. If `cargo ravenrs-lint` is missing, install it with `cargo install ravenrs-lint --locked`.

### Rules

- When a check fails, fix the code as the diagnostic's `help` says. Do not silence it.
- Never add `#[allow(...)]`, lower a level in `Cargo.toml` or `clippy.toml`, or write a `ravenrs-lint: allow(...)` comment to make a check pass. When an exception is truly right, use `#[expect(lint, reason = "...")]` or `// ravenrs-lint: allow(rule) reason`, and say so in your answer.
- Never use `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!` or indexing that can go out of bounds in the application. Return a `Result`, and show errors to the person in the interface.
- No `println!`, `eprintln!` or `dbg!` left in the code.
- Colors only from `Semantic` roles, text only from `TextStyle` steps. Never a literal `Color` or `font_size`.
- Padding, spacing and gaps are multiples of 4: screens 32, cards 24, stacks 16.
- One primary button per view; the others get `.style(ButtonStyle::Secondary)` or `Ghost`. Captions start with a verb.
- Every `IconButton` has a `.label(...)`.
- `State` lives in a field of the component, never created in `body`. `body` and `build` never read files, sleep or wait on the network.
- Small files and functions: split a file before it reaches 600 lines and a function before 80.
- Before using a RavenRS API, confirm it in the documentation or the sources; do not guess method names. If the framework lacks something, say so instead of building a lookalike.
- Every change to behavior comes with a test that drives it, through `Ui` for the interface.
<!-- ravenrs-lint:end -->
"

"
# Strict rules written by `cargo ravenrs-lint --init`. A lowered rule needs a reason a reviewer accepts.
[lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"
unused_must_use = "deny"
missing_debug_implementations = "deny"
rust_2018_idioms = { level = "deny", priority = -1 }

[lints.clippy]
all = { level = "deny", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "deny", priority = -1 }
# Pedantic rules that only add noise in an application.
module_name_repetitions = "allow"
must_use_candidate = "allow"
missing_errors_doc = "allow"
missing_panics_doc = "allow"
# No panics in the application: return errors and show them to the person.
unwrap_used = "deny"
expect_used = "deny"
panic = "deny"
todo = "deny"
unimplemented = "deny"
unreachable = "deny"
indexing_slicing = "deny"
string_slice = "deny"
# No leftovers from debugging.
dbg_macro = "deny"
print_stdout = "deny"
print_stderr = "deny"
# Every silenced lint says why, with #[expect(lint, reason = "...")].
allow_attributes = "deny"
allow_attributes_without_reason = "deny"
# Results and futures are never dropped by accident.
let_underscore_must_use = "deny"
# Functions stay small enough to read; the limits are in clippy.toml.
cognitive_complexity = "deny"
"

570.name: ravenrs_lint
570.docs:
Lints for applications built with [RavenRS](https://alexkads.github.io/RavenRS/).

The compiler and Clippy know Rust, not the rules an interface must follow to stay right in every
theme, for screen readers and across rebuilds. `ravenrs-lint` reads the syntax tree of an
application's sources and reports those rules the way the compiler does:

```text
error[ravenrs::raw_color]: literal color in the interface
  --> src/ui.rs:12:21
   |
12 |         .background(Color::rgb(0.1, 0.2, 0.3))
   |                     ^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = help: use a `Semantic` role, such as `.background(Semantic::Control)`, so it stays right in every theme
```

# Running it

From the command line, after `cargo install ravenrs-lint`:

```text
cargo ravenrs-lint            # every package of the workspace that depends on RavenRS
cargo ravenrs-lint --init     # recommended rustc and Clippy lints, the test below and AGENTS.md
```

From `cargo test`, so nothing passes while a rule is broken, with `ravenrs-lint` as a
dev-dependency and a file such as `tests/ravenrs_lint.rs`:

```no_run
#[test]
fn follows_the_ravenrs_rules() {
    ravenrs_lint::assert_clean();
}
```

# Configuring it

Levels follow Cargo's `[lints]`: `allow`, `warn` or `deny`. They go in the package's or the
workspace's metadata, and the package wins:

```toml
[package.metadata.ravenrs-lint]
language = "pt-BR"            # how button captions are checked: "en" (default) or "pt-BR"
extra-verbs = ["Ok"]          # first words accepted as verbs besides the built-in ones

[package.metadata.ravenrs-lint.lints]
off_grid_spacing = "deny"
```

A single place is excused with a comment that says why, on the same line or on its own line
right above:

```text
// ravenrs-lint: allow(raw_color) the church's logo keeps its brand color in every theme
```

`allow-file(...)` excuses the whole file. Test code (`#[test]`, `#[cfg(test)]`) is not checked.

The rules are listed in [`Lint`].
